accentPresets.constraint: Accent hues stay at least 35 degrees from the status hues (pass 155, fix ~95, approval ~50, reject ~12). No green, yellow, orange or red accent. Presets change hue and chroma only; lightness per step is fixed.
accentPresets.verifiedContrast: Measured on 2026-11-15 with sRGB clipping. Lowest values across all six presets: white on pane top 5.34 (sky); white on selected pane row 6.94; white on the primary button 4.95 (teal); accent-deep on white 7.72; active nav label 5.90. Night mode: on-accent text on accent 7.55 (plum); accent on card 6.54; light status inks on their chip fills at least 8.1.

narrative.overview:
An airy, light working app. The frame is white, the ground is a pale grey, and the ink is a deep navy. Work sits on white rounded cards, and one accent colour marks the primary action, the current place and the current step. The only saturated block of colour is a single accent gradient. On wide screens it fills the list pane of receipts.html; elsewhere it is reduced to the brand-mark circle. The step-3 verdict stays the loudest moment of a check: the result is pressed onto the page like the rubber stamps finance puts on paper documents (ตรายาง "จ่ายแล้ว", "ตรวจรับพัสดุ").

The person decides the mood, and the system guarantees the rest. There are six accents (sky by default, plus lavender, indigo, teal, plum and graphite) and three modes (light by default, dark, or follow the system). Every combination keeps the same structure, the same status colours and the same contrast floors, because the lightness of each accent step is fixed and only the hue and chroma change.

Density is relaxed and type is large because the readers include older researchers and people with weaker eyesight, on phones as often as on desktops. One family, Anuphan, sets both Thai and Latin. Status is always carried by a word and a drawn glyph as well as colour.

The system rejects a heavy, saturated shell (the indigo rail it replaced felt dense, "ทึบ") in favour of a light, open one ("โปร่ง"). It also rejects the editorial-serif look that came before.
keyCharacteristics: White side rail with a hairline divider on desktop. On phones, a white top bar and a white fixed bottom tab bar. All of these turn dark slate in night mode.
A pale grey ground, cards with soft shadows and deep navy ink. Night mode uses slate surfaces and light ink.
One accent, chosen by the user from six, computed from a single hue and chroma pair.
One saturated colour field: the accent-gradient list pane (and the brand-mark circle).
Five receipt statuses, each with its own soft fill, ink, dot, edge and drawn glyph, identical in every accent.
A rotated, double-ruled stamp for the step-3 verdict, used nowhere else.
Anuphan for everything, figures in tabular numerals.

rules.name: The Never-Colour-Alone Rule
rules.body: Every status shows its Thai word and its own drawn glyph (check, pencil, question, cross, clock) as well as its colour. This applies to chips (including chips on the pane), callouts, stat values and banners. A new status needs all four tokens (bg, ink, dot, edge), a glyph and a word.

rules.name: The Status-Distance Rule
rules.body: Accent hues stay at least 35° away from every status hue (pass 155, fix about 95, approval about 50, reject about 12), so an accent can never be read as a verdict. That is why there is no green, yellow, orange or red accent. The user's first request (orange, pink, green) was replaced for this reason, with the user's agreement. A new accent preset must clear the same distance.

rules.name: The Fixed-Lightness Rule
rules.body: An accent preset may change only `--accent-h` and `--accent-c`. Lightness per step is fixed in both themes, so the contrast checks done once hold for every accent. Don't give a preset its own lightness values.

rules.name: The One Colour Field Rule
rules.body: The shell is white (slate at night). The only saturated area in the system is the Pane gradient (`--color-pane`), and it appears in two places only: the receipts list pane and the brand-mark circle. Elsewhere the accent is limited to controls, the current place and focus. Don't paint the rail, page headers or content cards with the gradient. Any new pane must be a list or navigation surface that earns it.

rules.name: The White-on-Pane Legibility Rule
rules.body: All text on the pane is white and must reach at least 4.5:1 against the colour it actually sits on, in every accent and both themes, including overlays. Overlays on the pane therefore darken (black at 8 to 16%) and never lighten. If a change drops below the floor, darken the gradient. Don't make the text smaller or thinner.

rules.name: The Contract-Name Rule
rules.body: Every token name and class name in `style.css` is a contract with JS-generated markup and inline styles in `app/*.html` and `app/js/*.js`. Change values, never names. Themes and accents work by reassigning values to the same names. Older names are kept as aliases at the bottom of `:root`: `--color-stone`, `--color-sage`, `--color-warm-white`, `--color-surface-base/-sunken/-raised`, `--color-content-primary/-secondary/-tertiary`, `--color-border-default/-strong/-focus`, `--color-stone-hover/-active`, `--color-tooltip-bg`, the `--sp-1`…`--sp-8` spacing scale, and `--color-success/-error/-warning/-pending-*`. The `--color-accent-*` names (once indigo, then sky) and the `--color-rail*` names (now the white or slate shell) hold computed values. Alias, don't rename.

rules.name: The 14px Floor Rule
rules.body: Body copy is 16px, and no UI text goes below 14px. Inputs use 16px text (which also stops iOS from zooming on focus). This was adopted after review for older and low-vision readers.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Every amount, percentage, count and date uses tabular numerals so columns of baht figures line up. No separate monospace face.

rules.name: The Soft Shadow Rule
rules.body: Shadows are diffuse and fall downwards: blue-tinted in light mode, black-based in night mode. Never use hard offset shadows. The shell uses hairline dividers, not shadows (except the phone tab bar's faint upward edge).

rules.name: The Tinted-Panel Rule
rules.body: Explanation callouts and banners are tinted panels with a 1px status-edge border and a leading glyph. They never use a thick coloured side stripe.

dos: **Do** set every surface in Anuphan, with body text at 16px and nothing below 14px.
**Do** make inputs at least 46px tall with 16px text, and buttons at least 44px tall (52px for the large size).
**Do** give every status its word, its glyph and its bg/ink/dot/edge tokens. Use the dot colour only for non-text marks.
**Do** derive any new accent-coloured value from `--accent-h` and `--accent-c` with a fixed lightness, and define its night-mode value in `:root[data-theme="dark"]`.
**Do** keep every accent preset at least 35° from the status hues.
**Do** use `--color-on-accent` for text on solid accent fills and `--color-accent-deep` for accent text on white. Never hard-code white on accent.
**Do** keep the shell plain and separated by hairlines, and keep the Pane gradient to the list pane and the brand mark.
**Do** check white text on the pane at 4.5:1 or better, in all six accents and both themes, before shipping a pane change.
**Do** keep the verdict stamp the single loudest element on a result screen, and keep it to `#checkResult`.
**Do** put the primary action last in the markup of a right-aligned action row, so it sits on the right on desktop and on top when the row stacks on phones.
**Do** use tabular numerals for every amount, percentage, count and date.
**Do** change token values freely, but add aliases instead of renaming tokens or classes that JS or inline styles reference.
**Do** keep icons as inline line SVGs at a 1.8 stroke.
donts: **Don't** convey a status with colour alone, or invent a status colour without a glyph and a word.
**Don't** offer a green, yellow, orange or red accent, or any accent that could be mistaken for a verdict.
**Don't** give an accent preset its own lightness values, or hard-code a single accent hue in a component.
**Don't** bring back a saturated rail or top bar.
**Don't** spread the pane gradient onto headers, cards or backgrounds as decoration, or lighten it with white overlays.
**Don't** use the stamp treatment (rotation, double rule, stamp-in animation) on ordinary chips, badges or headings.
**Don't** use thick coloured side stripes on callouts or banners. Use the tinted panel with a leading glyph.
**Don't** pin anything tall over content on phones other than the bottom tab bar.
**Don't** bring back the serif display faces or a separate monospace face. Neither carries Thai.
**Don't** use emoji or text glyphs as icons.
